set.pl: Vejvoda strip across the S part of sec. 23 T36N R12W, Bear Lake Twp, north of the creek (1914 Standard Atlas; c.1918 Barron atlas)
pinev: Bear Lake Twp is T36N R12W: the 1914 Standard Atlas plate header and the c.1918 Barron County atlas plate ('T.36N. BEAR LAKE R.12W.') both show the Vejvoda strip in the S part of sec. 23; measured on the c.1918 plate against the BLM PLSS section box. Earlier R10W/R11W readings are withdrawn.
The farm is about 6 mi NNW of Rice Lake, not NE as the 1925 wire says; the plat and the 1920 Bear Lake Twp census win. The 1938-39 aerial check of this spot is still to do.

src: Atlas of Barron County, Wisconsin (c.1918), Bear Lake Twp plate (research/plat-barron/scans-c1918)

tw-mi-jennings-larson-hermit-gold.st: A 1923 AP story says the $10,000-75,000 in gold, received from Sweden, was buried by the hermit woodcutter John Larson 'near one of the outlying lakes'. His son John Jr. returned to search, and some thought the gold lay beneath the Jennings church, which was moved to Cadillac in 1923.
src: "Hunt Treasure on Site of Old Town / Hermit's Gold is Sought as Last Vestige of Jennings Goes", Ann Arbor Times News, 8 Jun 1923, p. 15 (AP); also Coldwater, 9 Jun 1923, and Flint Journal, 17 Jun 1923 (GenealogyBank)
